messages:
sre-bot: ALERT: autoscaler errors in aws/ap-southeast-2. Provision attempts for gpu-pool-04 are returning quota errors (ServiceQuotaExceeded). Queue length for inference requests up 8x, tail latency > 10s, some 429 throttles. Paging oncall.
Maya: saw the alerts, looking now. Which pool specifically?
Ajay: gpu-pool-04 (p3/gn6i mix) hitting two limits: GPU core quota and vCPU soft limit in account. Autoscaler got 'InsufficientInstanceCapacity' followed by 'ServiceQuotaExceeded'.
Ryan (oncall): I'm on it. Dropping into the autoscaler logs. Can someone post the exact API error?
deploy-bot: autoscaler: failed to create instance (RequestID: c7a2f...) -> ClientError: You have exceeded your quota for resource: gpu.p-cores in region ap-southeast-2.
Olivia: confirmed. Cloud console shows quota at 100% for NVIDIA GPUs and vCPU quota bumped by recent spikes from scheduled training jobs.
Isaac: customer impact - routing shows 12% of requests are hitting fallback and 7% returning 429s. Support ticket queue rising.
Maya: immediate mitigation plan: 1) Drain non-prod pools, 2) Shift low-priority inference traffic to ap-southeast-1, 3) Temporarily route to smaller model variants where acceptable. Who can do the region routing change?
Ajay: I can change routing rules. Will update the service policy to prefer ap-southeast-1 for new requests and mark ap-southeast-2 as degraded.
Ryan (oncall): start step 1 now — drain non-prod. Maya, tag which node groups to scale to 0.
Maya: tagging now: scale gp-nonprod-01, gp-spot-test to 0. Command: ```kubectl scale --replicas=0 deployment/gp-nonprod-01 -n inference```. Doing it. :spinner:
Olivia: I've opened a quota request with AWS Support for GPU cores and vCPUs (case 1234567890). ETA is unknown. Also checking if any unused reserved capacity can be popped in.
Isaac: Support message template posted to customer-facing status: "We're experiencing increased latency in ap-southeast-2 due to cloud GPU quota limits; mitigating by routing to other regions and prioritizing customer workloads. We'll post updates here."
Maya: Routing change in progress. Ajay, can you also enable model fallback to 8-bit quantized variant for non-critical routes?
Ajay: yes. Pushing policy update. Snippet: ```{ "route_preference": ["ap-southeast-1","ap-southeast-2"], "fallback_model": "gpt-small-q8" }``` Applying in 30s.
deploy-bot: rollout started -> policy:v2 -> 30% traffic to fallback model in other region.
Ryan (oncall): Observability: Maya, watch tail latency and queue size. Olivia, watch AWS case and reserved capacity. Ajay, monitor errors from autoscaler. I'll notify SRE pager if any further failures.
Maya: tail latency dropping from 10s to 3.2s after routing change. Queue length down ~60%. 429s decreasing. :slightly_smiling_face:
Olivia: AWS case updated: "Request received. We can expedite but likely 4-8 hours unless we provide justification." Adding note about production impact to expedite.
Isaac: Support updated customers flagged as P1 and those with contracts. Slack DM sent to account teams for any high-risk customers.
Ajay: autoscaler still logs occasional ServiceQuotaExceeded for retries. We added a backoff and a fallback to smaller instance types to accept partial capacity: ```aws ec2 run-instances --instance-type g4dn.xlarge || --instance-type g4dn.2xlarge``` (example).
Ryan (oncall): Good. Also enable prefix/KV caching for hot prefixes to reduce token throughput. Maya, can ops enable caching for the large prompt flows?
Maya: caching enabled for top 10 prefixes in ap-southeast-2 and ap-southeast-1. Config command: ```rwctl cache enable --prefix-list top10 --regions ap-southeast-1,ap-southeast-2```.
deploy-bot: cache rollout successful.
Olivia: I've also checked billing/reserved pools — we can move one dedicated pool from eu-west-1 for the next 4 hours as emergency capacity if we need it. Need approval.
Ryan (oncall): Approve. Move it and re-register to ap-southeast-2 via peering/failover path. Ajay, coordinate.
Ajay: spinning up network attachment and registering pool. If we hit quota again we'll cut new connections and route traffic to eu-west-1.
Maya: logging notes for postmortem: cause = unexpected GPU demand spike + quota limits not caught by runbook; detection = autoscaler and SLO alerts; mitigation = drain non-prod, cross-region routing, model fallback, caching, emergency dedicated pool+quota request.
Isaac: Customer impact summary for status page: "Partial service degradation in ap-southeast-2 between 03:12-04:05 UTC. Some users saw increased latency and intermittent throttling; ~5% of requests affected overall."
Ryan (oncall): handoff to next oncall @Ajay in 30m. Current state: traffic stabilized, queue reduced, retries/backoff in autoscaler in place. Keep monitoring for AWS case updates.
Maya: ack. I'll draft post-incident action items: 1) pre-authorize emergency dedicated pool moves, 2) automate quota-checks and simulated spike tests, 3) add autoscaler smarter fallbacks, 4) update runbook with explicit cross-region failover steps.
Olivia: I'll follow up with AWS support to shorten ETA and record the case details.
Isaac: closing note to support: sent status update to affected customers, monitoring for residual issues.
deploy-bot: INCIDENT: resolved (stabilized) - incident_id: inc-20240405-09. Duration: ~53 minutes.
Ryan (oncall): closing thread, will raise postmortem. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
